Posterior Mean of the Baseline Per-Period Event Probability Given History

Source: R/G2G_varying_posterior_functions.R
G2G_varying_posterior_p0.Rd

Updates the population distribution of the baseline rate using a customer's observed history and returns the posterior mean of the baseline per-period event probability \(p_0 = 1 - e^{-\lambda}\), i.e. the per-period event probability at covariate value zero (the reference levels of any factors).

Usage

G2G_varying_posterior_p0(solution, X_hist = NULL)

Arguments

solution

A fitted model of class "G2Gcov" returned by G2G_varying_MLE. Its par holds r, alpha and the coefficients on the original covariate scale (alpha already absorbs the centering used in fitting), so X_mat needs no centering or scaling.

X_hist

Covariate values for each period the customer has survived, one row per period (t = 1, ..., T), in any of the forms accepted by X_mat in G2G_varying_survival. The history must contain only event-free periods. NULL (no history) returns the prior mean.

Value

A single number: the posterior mean of the baseline per-period event probability given survival through the full history.

Details

A customer who survived t periods with covariate path \(z(1), \dots, z(t)\) has posterior \(\lambda \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(r, \alpha + C(t))\), where \(C(t) = \sum_{j=1}^{t} e^{z(j)\beta'}\). The posterior mean of \(p_0\) is then $$1 - \left(\frac{\alpha + C(t)}{\alpha + C(t) + 1}\right)^r.$$ The history enters only through \(C(t)\).

Examples

# \donttest{
  data(kb_data)
  kb_data$status <- 1L - kb_data$censor
  fit <- G2G_varying_MLE(
    "Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp",
    data    = kb_data,
    subject = "id"
  )
  # A customer who has survived the first 8 weeks
  hist <- kb_data[kb_data$id == kb_data$id[1], c("coupon", "anyp")][1:8, ]
  G2G_varying_posterior_p0(fit, hist)
